event_name: Start of US and Israeli military action against Iran; tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz largely stops
capacity_note: EIA: 7.5 million b/d of Gulf production shut in during March 2026 (Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain). IEA: flows through the strait fell from about 20 million b/d to an average of 2.7 million b/d in March to May. Production shut-ins and strait flows are different measures.
source_2_publisher: AP (via Michigan Public, May 8, 2026): 'launched the war on Feb. 28'
notes: Feb 28, 2026 was a Saturday; day zero is the next trading day. IEA commentary (June 22, 2026) gives the strait flow figures: https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-global-oil-supplies-have-readjusted-to-help-fill-the-huge-gap-left-by-the-strait-of-hormuz-shock

event_name: Iran's Revolutionary Guards state the Strait of Hormuz is closed; major shipping lines suspend transits
capacity_note: No separate volume; part of the W01 disruption.
notes: Reports place the declaration on March 1 or March 2. Caixin is a news outlet, not an agency: replace with Reuters/AP/AFP or an official notice when checking. Wikipedia (pointer) cites March 2.

event_name: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation declares force majeure and cuts crude output
capacity_note: KPC did not say how much it would cut. Kuwait produced about 2.6 million b/d of crude in February.
source_1_publisher: Reuters (Yousef Saba, Trixie Yap) via TimesLIVE
notes: Location is approximate (central Kuwait), for the map only.

event_name: Saudi Arabia cuts crude output by about 2 million b/d to about 8 million b/d (Safaniya and Zuluf offshore fields shut)
capacity_note: Reuters, two sources: output cut by about 2 million b/d to around 8 million b/d after the two fields were shut. Some exports diverted to Yanbu on the Red Sea.
notes: E17 uses March 13 (date of the report EIA links to). A Bloomberg video dated March 9 says Saudi Arabia began output cuts as storage filled: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-03-09/saudi-arabia-begins-oil-output-cuts-as-storage-fills-up-video . Starter row's cause was 'attack'; changed to 'blockade' because the source attributes the cut to the closed strait. Check both.

event_name: UAE crude output falls by more than half as ADNOC shuts in production
capacity_note: Reported as 'more than half' with no figure in the summary read. OPEC data later put March output at 1.89 million b/d. Not converted to a volume.
notes: EVENTS_NOTES.md lead. Location approximate (Abu Dhabi onshore fields), for the map only. The Fujairah terminal attack is a separate lead without a confirmed date.

event_name: Iraq declares force majeure on oilfields developed by foreign companies; Basra output cut to 0.9 million b/d
capacity_note: Oil minister: Basra Oil Company production cut to 900,000 b/d from 3.3 million b/d. The 2.4 million is the difference of those two stated figures.
notes: The ministry letter is dated March 17; Reuters reported it March 20. E18 used March 20 and a 3 million figure from Wikipedia; this row uses the Reuters figures. Choose the date by when the market could know (likely March 20).

event_name: US and Iran announce a two-week ceasefire; Iran agrees to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
notes: Announced the evening of April 7 US time, which was April 8 in the Gulf (Wikipedia gives April 8). Day zero is probably April 8. Replace with an agency or official source (e.g. a White House or Pakistan government statement) when checking.

event_name: US forces begin a blockade of ships entering or leaving Iranian ports
facility_or_route: Iranian ports (Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman)
capacity_note: No volume stated. CENTCOM says ships transiting Hormuz to and from non-Iranian ports were not to be impeded.
notes: Began April 13 at 10 a.m. ET per CENTCOM. Map point is Bandar Abbas, approximate.

event_name: Iran declares the Strait of Hormuz open to commercial vessels for the rest of the ceasefire
capacity_note: No volume. Conditions: commercial ships only, on Iran's designated route, coordinated with Iranian forces. The US blockade of Iranian ports stayed in place.
notes: Reported price reaction: Brent June futures -10.42%, WTI May -11.11% (as reported; verify against the price table).

event_name: US extends the ceasefire with Iran while keeping the blockade of Iranian ports
notes: Announced a day before the two-week truce was due to expire. A later 60-day extension was reported in late May pending approval; not a separate row.

event_name: US and Iran sign the Islamabad memorandum to end hostilities and reopen the strait
capacity_note: A supply-returning event. Reported terms include reopening the strait and temporarily waiving US sanctions on Iranian oil.
notes: Signed digitally over June 17 and 18; EIA pages disagree by a day (E19 note). Arab News Pakistan also reports the signing: https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2647648

event_name: Iran announces the Strait of Hormuz closed again, citing ceasefire violations
capacity_note: No volume. Recorded as a risk event: whether transits actually fell can be checked against chokepoint_transit.
notes: June 20, 2026 was a Saturday; day zero is the next trading day. physical_supply_lost set to 'no' pending a check of PortWatch transits.

event_name: Three tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz; US strikes follow early the next day
capacity_note: No volume figure in the sources. Vessel damage reported; no barrels-per-day loss stated.
notes: Ship strikes July 7 (reported by the UK military's UKMTO); US strikes and the truce breakdown early July 8 (Wikipedia pointer uses July 8). EIA names July 7. The US also revoked a license for Iranian oil sales the same day.

event_name: Attacks on more than a dozen vessels near the Strait of Hormuz; Brent closes above $100 the next day
capacity_note: No volume figure in the sources.
notes: EIA: Brent futures exceeded $100 on Sept 9 and peaked at $109 on Sept 15. News reports: Brent settled $99.49 on Sept 9 and closed $107.63 on Sept 10 (Nation Thailand: https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40070894). EIA likely refers to an intraday high. EIA also mentions pipeline attacks affecting Saudi supply this quarter, without dates.
